author: val
body: The operands are chosen to separate three states, not two. A source of only '1. alpha' passes whether the number is parsed or hardcoded to 1, because the right answer and the wrong answer coincide there. '2. beta' separates parsed from hardcoded; '17. seventeen' additionally separates a real text-to-integer from a single-digit shortcut. Row 0 stays because it is the one row neither defect can move.

author: val
body: The bullet and the plain line are controls: unordered lists and paragraphs were never broken, so they say the parser still works at all. Without them a parser that recognised nothing would report clean ordered output by reporting no output.

author: val
body: The first line prints the CCE code points the chapter under test depends on, so the day CCE's digit band moves this test says WHY it went red instead of only that it did. Measured 2026-07-28 against seed 7C2FF75D: digit0=3 digit9=12 dot=65 space=2, against the 51..61 the source had assumed.

author: val
body: Both sabotages fired on exactly their own rows against seed 7C2FF75D. Restoring the 51..61 digit band turns rows 0-2 into para[...] and leaves the bullet and paragraph alone. Restoring the hardcoded UiMdOrderedItem 1 moves rows 1 and 2 to num=1 and leaves row 0, the bullet and the paragraph alone.
